claim_boundary: Theorem/proof-sketch and external falsification plan only; no physical GR/EFE/full ADM/physical spacetime/physical curvature.
theorem_candidate: Recoverability under pruning requires retained source-origin information.
proof_sketch: If reconstruction R(P(T(x0))) recovers sigma with error <= epsilon, then the compressed observation Y=P(T(x0)) must distinguish source classes well enough to support that reconstruction.
By Fano-style reasoning, low error implies a lower bound on mutual information between source assignment Sigma and observation Y.
Therefore successful recovery under pruning requires retained source-origin information above I_min, up to the looseness of the estimator and finite-sample assumptions.
The simulations do not prove the theorem universally; they test whether the implication is violated under controlled synthetic perturbations.
external_falsifiers: Find a system that reconstructs causal/source assignment after pruning with E_R <= epsilon while measured I_source <= I_min.
Show reconstruction succeeds after source-origin information is destroyed while transport, continuity, H-like, or geometry-like summaries are preserved.
Show the theorem fails under an independent reconstruction operator not used in this work.
Show the information estimator overstates retained source-origin information.
safe_statement: In synthetic finite-graph recoverability tests, successful reconstruction after pruning required retained source-origin information under the frozen theorem test.
